request.spec:
A DRAFT claim can be deleted (a button on the claim; any other status, or a claim in a closed
period, is refused with an error on the claim): its status becomes DELETED, it counts nowhere (not
in any total, not in the status counts of the header or the summary), it cannot be edited, opened
or voided, its log gains a DELETED line, and CLAIM_DELETED is written naming the claim. On the same
sheet-today it was deleted, a restore button makes it a DRAFT again (CLAIM_RESTORED, a DRAFT line in
the log); on a later day the restore is refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A DRAFT claim can be deleted (a button on the claim; any other status, or a claim in a closed
period, is refused with an error on the claim): its status becomes DELETED, it counts nowhere (not
in any total, not in the status counts of the header or the summary), it cannot be edited, opened
or voided, its log gains a DELETED line, and CLAIM_DELETED is written naming the claim. On the same
sheet-today it was deleted, a restore button makes it a DRAFT again (CLAIM_RESTORED, a DRAFT line in
the log); on a later day the restore is refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Deleting and restoring draft claims now works. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the acceptance spec.

**Server**
- `ClaimStatus` has a new status, `DELETED`. Only a DRAFT can be deleted, and only a DELETED claim can go back to DRAFT. The audit lines are `CLAIM_DELETED` and `CLAIM_RESTORED`. Opening, voiding, settling, editing and reassigning were already limited to other statuses, so they refuse a DELETED claim without any change.
- `DeleteClaim` refuses any claim that isn't a DRAFT. It also refuses a claim whose due-by date falls inside a closed period, which is how the app already decides "in a closed period". That's why the test's claim dated 2026-02-05 can be deleted even though period P1 is closed: its due-by date is later than the period.
- `RestoreClaim` only works on the same sheet-today as the claim's latest `DELETED` line in its log. A new `ClaimLogRepository.deletedOn` looks that date up.
- Two new endpoints, `claims/{claimId}/delete.POST.yml` and `restore.POST.yml`, run the same steps as void: save, add the log line, write the audit record, roll up.
- A deleted claim can't gain a proof, and it is skipped when a new holiday shifts due-by dates.
- No database migration was needed, because the existing status column already fits `DELETED`.

**Front end**
- Each claim has `claim-delete` and `claim-restore` buttons, and a refusal shows `claim-error` on the claim.
- A deleted claim counts in no total or status count. The totals already ignore DRAFT and VOID claims, and the header and summary only count the five existing statuses.

**One thing to check:** I changed the audit name for moving a claim to DRAFT from `CLAIM_DRAFTED` to `CLAIM_RESTORED`. Nothing else in the app moved a claim to DRAFT, so restore is the only thing that writes it.

I also chose not to check closed periods on restore, because the request only mentions the same-day rule. If a period closes after a claim is deleted, the claim can still be restored that same day.
